expectation: ICOS is a membrane marker on a subset of activated CD4 T cells (Tfh, Treg). Expect sparse, discrete membrane-ringed cells, scattered or clustered in lymphoid aggregates and T-cell zones, mostly on CD3+ cells, with little signal elsewhere.
observed: A: many discrete yellow single-cell dots across most tissue cores, denser in aggregates, while a few cores (row 2 right, row 3 second) show diffuse haze. B and C: mostly empty with faint grain, one or two cells. D: a bright cell with a clear membrane ring. E: ICOS clusters sit within CD3-dense areas, and white overlap marks co-expression.
why: ICOS marks a sparse, discrete subset of cells with membrane rings that cluster in CD3-rich aggregates, as expected for activated T cells.
notes: Discrete ICOS-positive cells with membrane rings are scattered across the tissue and concentrate in lymphoid-like aggregates. In the E row they overlap CD3. Two cores show diffuse haze, but this does not outweigh the cellular pattern.
